title: Online, low-volume meditation does not alter immune-related biomarkers
authors: Graham B, Jin Y, Bazeley P, Husni E, Calabrese LH.
summary: The trial found no significant between-group differences in the prespecified immune-related gene set, wider RNA expression or other tested biomarkers. Stress improved earlier in the music group and later in the mindfulness group.
limitation: A small trial of brief online practice in otherwise healthy nurses. The result concerns this dose and delivery; it does not establish the absence of effects from other programmes.

title: Community singing intervention reduces maternal salivary cytokines and enhances maternal-infant cortisol synchrony in postnatal depression: biological findings from the SHAPER-PND trial
authors: Kirkpatrick M, Priestley K, Bind RH, Rebecchini L, Borsini A, Estevao C, Hazelgrove K, Laijawala R, Alford S, Woods AJ, Crane N, Manoharan M, Burton A, Dye H, Osborn T, Greenwood L, Dazzan P, Fancourt D, Pariante C.
design: Biomarker analysis within a randomized trial
summary: After the first community-singing session, salivary IL-6 decreased by 26% in the singing group. The time-by-group interaction for IL-6 was significant. Later analyses also examined mother–infant cortisol synchrony and communication.
limitation: This measured salivary cytokine protein, not IL6 transcription. The biological subset was unbalanced, and speech correlations do not isolate the causal effect of particular words.

title: Preoperative binaural beats reduce remimazolam dosage and enhance safety in anesthesia induction: A randomized controlled trial.
authors: Kim HC, Sohn JY, Kim MH, Kim YJ, Chang CH, Seo JH.
summary: In 72 surgical patients, 30 minutes of 1 Hz binaural beats reduced the mean remimazolam dose required for loss of consciousness from 17.7 to 15.0 mg; hypotension occurred in 6% versus 28% of participants.
limitation: A single-centre anaesthesia study with no auditory intervention in the comparison arm. EEG differences were not significant, so the proposed entrainment mechanism remains unconfirmed.

title: Effects of preoperative binaural beats on the propofol dose for induction of general anesthesia: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
authors: Kim YJ, Choe HW, Yoon SB, Lee H, Kim HS, Seo JH.
summary: Among 69 surgical patients, 20 minutes of 1 Hz binaural beats reduced the mean propofol dose needed to stop responding to verbal commands from 105 to 87 mg; the difference was -18 mg, with a 95% confidence interval of -32 to -5 mg.
limitation: Anxiety and frontal EEG bands did not differ significantly. This supports an anaesthetic-dose finding within the tested clinical protocol, rather than a general claim of brainwave entrainment.

title: Binaural Beats Reduce Postoperative Morphine Consumption in Older adults After Total Knee Replacement Surgery.
journal: Alternative therapies in health and medicine
authors: Tani A, Vagheggini G, Moretti F, Del Colombo V, Lehle J, Campana S, Labate A, Tomaiuolo F.
summary: In 40 older adults undergoing knee replacement, preoperative 4 Hz binaural beats reduced first-day self-administered morphine from 11.85 to 5.75 mg compared with matched tones presented at the same frequency to both ears.
limitation: Pain ratings did not differ between groups. This small, single-centre trial supports an opioid-consumption finding in a specific surgical protocol, with broader effectiveness still requiring replication.
